questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A safe country to stay, high quality education and interesting modules with great academic outcomes, cultural diversity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, it was an excellent experience with unforgettable memories! The modules I took were very interesting and instructive! However, it was a bit challenging to prepare for the exams as examples of exam questions from previous years were not provided.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, the staff at the university were helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Check-in procedures at my accommodation on-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was no orientation week this semester but it could have been useful! Instead, all information were sent to our emails and we could also help each other in the exchange groupchat on WhatsApp.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could not choose between different housing types, as I was offered an accommodation in a residential college: College of Alice and Peter Tan (CAPT).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plans were compulsory at CAPT and cooking facilities were available. Every three floors shared one pantry.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was very convenient and definitely a cheaper option! It was a great opportunity to experience campus life and interact with local students as well as exchangers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall my stay at CAPT was fantastic and there were a lot of social activities to join during the semester! Unfortunately I was very sensitive to noise so it was difficult to sleep, especially in the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy. Even without orientation week it was easy to navigate through the registration process. I used the module registration student guide provided by the university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Firstly, you submit module requests for these modules preapproved by UCPH. You should attach your transcript to show that you meet the prerequisites (if needed).
If you don't get all of the modules that you wanted, it is possible to request for other modules in the following rounds.
If you find out later that you don't like the modules allocated to you, there is an add/drop period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The module registration student guide and Registrar's Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get all the modules I requested. However, I switched one of the modules allocated to me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Check the vacancy report provided by the university when selecting modules.
If you really want to read a module but there is no vacancy, you should contact the course coordinator directly as he/she might allow you to take the module anyway!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The programme had a high academic standard and the modules I took were very interesting and relevant to my programme at UCPH.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I was a master student, UCPH allowed me to read modules of at least level 4000 which were considered as undergraduate modules at NUS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Majority of the modules at NUS had continuous assessments, therefore midterms, assignments and presentation throughout the semester. Both continuous assessments and final exams accounted for the total grades.
Compared to UCPH, the reading materials were less at NUS but the workload was still high.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LSM4213 Systems Neurobiology
LSM4214 Cancer Pharmacology
LSM4221 Drug Discovery and Clinical Trials
LSM4226 Infection and Immunity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Cancer Pharmacology and Drug Discovery and Clinical Trials.
Personally, I think both modules were very interesting and relevant to pharmacy, and the professors were great!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Consultation fee at a clinic and medications.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Foods at Science Canteen on campus were very cheap!
Generally alcohol is very expensive in Singapore!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were great opportunities to explore the city and plenty of social activities on campus!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A wide range of activities such as tennis, soccer, dancing, cheerleading and bands.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You should try to join different clubs/organisations for all NUS students based on your personal interests! If you stay in a residential college, I highly recommend to join some of the interest groups as it is a good opportunity to make new friends!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Try Singaporean local foods at Hawker Centres!
Visit Gardens by the Bay, Cloud Forrest and Art Science Museum.
Travel to other countries nearby, such as Indonesia and Malaysia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Singapore is a very multicultural country with different ethnic groups. It has a good combination of Asian and European culture. There are many rules in Singapore, but in general, if you just use common sense everything should be fine!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay on-campus and join the social activities! Although majority of local students are competitive, they are very friendly!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural diversity. Furthermore, Singapore is an extremely clean and safe city!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have a positive mind as the workload can be high and it might be difficult to adapt to a whole new enviroment. 
2. Use your free time to explore the city and the many options of delicious foods.
3. Socialize with both local students and exchangers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: For majority of the modules at NUS, continuous assessments are very common so you should study throughout the whole semester and not only during the reading weeks. But you would still have time to do social activities!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I learned to have a positive mindset even in the critical situations.
I met many people with different backgrounds and I made good new friends from both Singapore and other countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be far away from home in Denmark and to study in a whole new environment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange in Singapore! It is a wonderful experience and you wouldn't regret it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
